question: Why is the son of Śiva unforgettable as he wards off obstacles?
premises: He wards off obstacles with claps of his own ears.
He is the son of the enemy of Anaṅga.
The question implies he cannot be forgotten.
inference: No one would forget the son of Śiva, who wards off obstacles with the clapping of his ears.
plain_english: Who would forget the son of the enemy of Anaṅga, warding off obstacles with the claps of his own ears?
